outcome: Give farm operations director / food quality head a governed method to improve verified disease outbreak lead time using field images, disease labels and weather history, with final decisions…
overview: Crop Disease Early Warning from Imagery addresses teams rely on lagging aggregates when forecasts or decisions depend on changing operational conditions in agriculture and food production operations. The first proof of value uses field images, disease labels and weather history. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is verified disease outbreak lead time, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: field images, disease labels and weather history; define verified disease outbreak lead time and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Farm Operations Director / Food Quality Head.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including backtest across seasonal and peak periods with a holdout cohort.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
